subject: tasks.records

recordTypes.summary: Machine-readable Task creation, assignment, date, lifecycle, and Project-promotion rules selected from one definition authority.

fields.summary: The exact human-readable Tasks policy title.
Whether each exact Task create batch requires operator confirmation.
The bounded number of Task candidates inspected before create.
The portable Task fields used for deterministic duplicate review.
The portable lifecycle state assigned to a newly captured Task.
The closed portable Task context vocabulary.
Whether the selected Task workflow requires one exact Project relation.
The portable rule limiting assignment to the authenticated current actor or no assignee.

content.summary: The normalized Tasks rules contain no portable body content.

recordTypes.summary: A bounded work item that can be related to one or more projects.

fields.summary: The task title describing the intended work.
The exact related project record identity used for bounded project-status queries.
Exact provider-scoped person identities for the assigned operators.
The pinned calendar date for the task's next action.
Exact source meeting resource identities whose grounded work was folded into this task.
Exact bounded source excerpts supporting the folded task outcome.
Content fingerprints of private review summaries that grounded the fold without assuming a provider-created record identity.

content.summary: Task records have no portable body content.

limitations: The governed context.tasks vocabulary artifact owns portable Task terminology; compatibility pointers and provider labels are non-canonical projections.
This model owns portable Tasks, assignees, dates, lifecycle, Task policy, and grounded source relationships; Projects, CRM, and Meetings remain separate selectable Context packs.
Project and Meeting links are optional typed resource identities. A standalone Task does not require either Context pack.
A particular Automation policy may require one exact Project even though the portable Task model does not.
Provider-scoped assignee identifiers remain explicit workspace identity references and never become CRM contacts by implication.
Task creation and updates require separate Automation, Integration, configuration, approval, checkpoint, and verification authority.
